questions.question: What was Walt Disney's full birth name?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his full name as 'Walter Elias Disney'.
Incorrect. 'Walt Disney' is a shortened version of his name, not his full birth name.
Incorrect. 'Walter Disney' omits his middle name, Elias.
Incorrect. 'Elias Disney' was his father's name, not his.

questions.question: In which city was Walt Disney born?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says he was born in Chicago, Illinois.
Incorrect. Kansas City is where he later lived and worked, not where he was born.
Incorrect. Los Angeles is where he moved to in 1923, not his birthplace.
Incorrect. Marceline, Missouri is where he spent part of his childhood, not his birthplace.

questions.question: Who did Walt Disney develop the character Mickey Mouse with?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states he developed Mickey Mouse with Ub Iwerks.
Incorrect. Roy Disney was his brother and business partner, but not the co-creator of Mickey Mouse.
Incorrect. Fred Harman was an early business partner, but not involved in creating Mickey Mouse.
Incorrect. Walter Pfeiffer was a childhood friend who introduced him to vaudeville, not a collaborator on Mickey Mouse.

questions.question: What was the name of the first highly popular success that Walt Disney created in 1928?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Mickey Mouse was 'his first highly popular success'.
Incorrect. Oswald the Lucky Rabbit was a successful series, but Mickey Mouse is described as his first highly popular success.
Incorrect. Alice's Wonderland was an early film, but not his first highly popular success.
Incorrect. Snow White was a later feature film, not his first success.

questions.question: What was the name of the theme park that Walt Disney opened in Anaheim, California in 1955?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states he opened Disneyland in Anaheim, California in July 1955.
Incorrect. Disney World was a different theme park he began developing later, not the one opened in 1955.
Incorrect. EPCOT was a planned city, not the theme park opened in 1955.
Incorrect. The Moscow Fair was an event he helped plan, not a theme park.

questions.question: What was the name of the city that Walt Disney planned to build as part of the Disney World project?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article mentions the 'Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow' (EPCOT) as the heart of Disney World.
Incorrect. Disneyland is the theme park in California, not the planned city.
Incorrect. Anaheim is the city where Disneyland is located, not the planned city.
Incorrect. Marceline is the town in Missouri where he spent his childhood, not the planned city.

questions.question: What was the cause of Walt Disney's death in 1966?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states he 'died of lung cancer' in 1966.
Incorrect. Tuberculosis is mentioned as the illness his brother Roy was convalescing from, not his own cause of death.
Incorrect. A heart attack is not mentioned as the cause of his death.
Incorrect. The article specifically gives lung cancer as the cause, not old age.

questions.question: Which of these films received five Academy Awards?
options: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Mary Poppins (1964) 'received five Academy Awards'.
Incorrect. Snow White is mentioned as an early feature, but not as receiving five Academy Awards.
Incorrect. Pinocchio is mentioned as an early feature, but not as receiving five Academy Awards.
Incorrect. Bambi is mentioned as an early feature, but not as receiving five Academy Awards.

questions.question: Where did Walt Disney spend what he described as one of the happiest and most formative periods of his life?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says he described his childhood in Marceline as 'one of the happiest and most formative periods of his life'.
Incorrect. Chicago is his birthplace, but not the place he described as happiest.
Incorrect. Kansas City is where he later worked, but not the place he described as happiest.
Incorrect. Hollywood is where he moved for his career, but not the place he described as happiest.

questions.question: What was the name of the studio that Walt Disney and his brother Roy set up in the early 1920s?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says they set up the Disney Brothers Studio (now the Walt Disney Company).
Incorrect. Laugh-O-Gram Studio was an earlier venture in Kansas City, not the one set up with Roy.
Incorrect. Iwerks-Disney Commercial Artists was a short-lived business with Ub Iwerks, not with Roy.
Incorrect. The Walt Disney Studio was established later in 1926, not the initial studio set up with Roy.
